english.title: Duty of person responsible for animal to ensure welfare - Animal Welfare Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) did not take such steps as were reasonable in all the circumstances to ensure that the needs of an animal for which you were responsible, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ANIMAL..), were met to the extent required by good practice in that **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE(S)..)

english.notes:
(i) See section 9(2) for a list of the needs of an animal.
(ii) See section 9(3) for the "relevant" circumstances.
(iii) Section 9(4) provides that nothing in this section applies to the destruction of an animal in an appropriate and humane manner.
(iv) See section 33 for privation orders.
(v) See section 34 disqualification from owning keeping animals.
(vi) See section 35 for power to seize animals in connection with disqualification.
(vii) See section 37 for destruction in the interests of the animal.

other.timelimitforprosecutions: Complex see section 31 of the Act
other.penalty:
Summary: 51 weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

NOTE:
Section 32(5) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that In relation to an offence committed before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 the reference to 51 weeks is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Time Limit on Prosecutions:
Complex see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
